title: Agentic Persona Manifest
description: The single index-of-record for one agentic persona. It ties together the persona's identity, the definition layer(s) that implement it, the skills it uses, its trigger surface, its trust/permission posture, its eval gate, and a pointer to its canary-rings entry. The manifest does NOT duplicate ring membership or gate knobs — those live in petry-projects/.github standards/canary-rings.json (the single source of truth). See standards/persona-standards.md.

allOf.description: A persona that ships a dedicated reusable workflow (runtime.reusable) MUST carry a canary block for ring registration. See ADR-0006.
A persona with a canary block MUST declare runtime.reusable — shared-runtime personas served by the persona-runner MUST omit canary entirely. See ADR-0006.

then.description: A persona at status 'stable' MUST carry an evals block (the held-out gate). See persona-standards.md §1.
A persona that enables the 'mention' surface MUST declare how it is addressed. See persona-standards.md §4.1.

schema_version.description: Manifest schema version. Bump only when the schema shape changes in a backwards-incompatible way; additive optional fields stay at v1.

id.description: Stable kebab-case identifier. MUST be a ROLE, never a person name — 'qa-lead', not 'murat' (persona-standards.md §1.6). MUST equal the persona directory name, the addressing team slug in `address.handle`, AND the channel-tag agent name used in canary-rings.json (e.g. 'qa-lead', 'dev-lead').

name.description: Human display name for the ROLE (e.g. 'QA Lead', 'Dev Lead'). MUST NOT be a person name, even when this persona wraps an upstream framework agent that has one. Upstream agents are referenced ONLY by their technical skill id (definition.layers[].framework.skill, e.g. 'bmad-tea'); their persona names are upstream's business and are not mirrored here. See persona-standards.md §1.6.

title.description: Role title (e.g. 'Master Test Architect & Quality Advisor').

summary.description: One-sentence statement of what this persona is for.

status.description: Lifecycle stage. 'draft' = not yet cut; canary/ring0/ring1/stable mirror the furthest channel this persona has been promoted to; 'retired' = decommissioned.

owner.description: Owning team in 'org/team' form (matches CODEOWNERS). Team-based ownership only, per codeowners-standard.md.

definition.description: Where and how the persona is actually implemented. A persona MUST declare at least one layer. Per persona-standards.md §Definition, the manifest is the unifier ON TOP of these layers — it points at them, it does not replace them.

layers.description: Ordered list of definition layers that implement this persona.

kind.description: framework-agent: a vendored framework agent (BMAD etc.). copilot-profile: an agents/<name>.md profile. workflow-prompts: a prompts/<persona>/ library driven by a shell orchestrator. gh-aw: a GitHub Agentic Workflow .md compiled to a .lock.yml.

path.description: Repo-relative path to the layer's root (the SKILL.md dir, the profile .md, the prompts dir, or the gh-aw .md).

framework.description: Required when kind == 'framework-agent'. Records the upstream provenance and pin so the manifest can point INTO the framework rather than fork it.

vendor_pin.description: Vendored version/tag, MUST match the framework's VENDOR.md (e.g. 'v1.19.0').

skill.description: The framework skill/agent id backing this persona (e.g. 'bmad-tea'). This is the ONLY handle we keep on an upstream agent: a technical id, never the persona name upstream may give it. If you need to know what upstream calls it, read upstream.

local_overrides.description: Local customization applied on top of a vendored layer (never hand-edit vendored files). Overrides that would benefit upstream should be flagged for contribution back.

path.description: Repo-relative path to the override file(s) (e.g. a customize.toml overlay or an orchestration wrapper).

upstream_candidate.description: true if this override is a general improvement that SHOULD be proposed back to the upstream framework rather than kept local forever.

address.description: How a human addresses this persona from a comment (`@<handle>`). REQUIRED when the 'mention' surface is enabled. See persona-standards.md §4.1. There is deliberately NO `aliases` field — see §4.1.1 'Renames'.

handle.description: The addressing handle in 'org/team-slug' form, mentioned as '@org/team-slug'. MUST be an org TEAM, never a user account: GitHub's user namespace is global and first-come, so a bare '@qa-lead' resolves to an unrelated real account and notifies a stranger on every mention (verified: qa-lead, dev-lead, scrum-master are all live accounts). An org team slug cannot collide. The slug MUST equal `id`, so routing is a prefix-strip — which also makes handle uniqueness a theorem rather than a check (org is pinned, slug == id, id == the persona directory name, directory names are unique). Team must be privacy 'closed' (secret teams are unmentionable) with notification_setting 'notifications_disabled'; those are live properties CI verifies, not shape this schema can check.

skills.description: Capabilities the persona can invoke, consumed by path (vendor-neutral). Advisory index for humans; the authoritative wiring is inside the definition layers.

triggers.description: The trigger matrix — the checklist of every surface this persona may act on. Per persona-standards.md §Triggers, default is advisory (read-only) everywhere; write access is opt-in per surface and MUST carry a gate label and a trust floor.

default_mode.description: The mode for any surface not explicitly listed. MUST be 'advisory' or 'off' — write is never a default, only an explicit per-surface opt-in.

opt_out_label.description: Label that opts an item out of this persona entirely (convention: '<id>:hands-off').

surface.description: The work-item surface / GitHub event family.

events.description: Specific event actions in scope (e.g. ['opened','labeled'] for issues).

mode.description: advisory: comments/reviews/labels only, no code changes. write: opens/pushes PRs or mutates repo content.

gate_label.description: REQUIRED when mode == 'write': the label that arms the persona on this surface (e.g. 'dev-lead').

trust_floor.description: Minimum author_association allowed to trigger on this surface. Defaults to trust.author_association_floor when omitted.

bridge.description: Optional repository_dispatch/workflow_dispatch bridge type when the surface cannot run the agent inline (e.g. 'discussion' events).

trust.description: Trust boundary applied before the persona consumes agent quota.

author_association_floor.description: The default set of author associations allowed to trigger the persona. Convention: [OWNER, MEMBER, COLLABORATOR].

runtime.description: How the persona is wired into CI. Optional for advisory-only personas that run entirely inside an existing workflow.

host.description: Repo that owns the reusable (matches canary-rings.json host).

reusable.description: Repo-relative path to the reusable workflow, if any.

caller_stub.description: Repo-relative path to the thin caller stub.

run_workflow.description: Display name of the workflow whose run history feeds the health gate. MUST match canary-rings.json run_workflow for this id.

permissions.description: The full permission set the reusable requests. The caller stub MUST grant a superset of this or the fleet gets startup_failure.

identity.description: The GitHub account this persona ACTS AS at runtime — the login it commits/pushes/reviews/comments as, and the Actions secret holding that account's PAT. This is deliberately distinct from `address.handle` (the org TEAM humans @-mention): the handle routes a mention, the identity authenticates the work. Making it declarative here is what stops two personas from silently sharing one machine user via a single `vars.BOT_USER` variable (the dev-lead→donpetry-bot regression). The runtime resolves `BOT_USER` from `identity.account`; CI asserts the workflow's credential reference matches `identity.credential`. The companion validator (`validate-personas.py`) further enforces that `credential` follows the `GH_PAT_<ACCOUNT>[_<QUALIFIER>]` naming convention (where `<ACCOUNT>` is the login upper-snake-cased), while accepting grandfathered account-named secrets such as `DON_PETRY_BOT_GH_PAT`.

account.description: GitHub login this persona acts as (commits/pushes/reviews/comments). A user or machine-user account, NOT a team. e.g. 'don-petry' (dev-lead) or 'donpetry-bot' (pr-review).

credential.description: Name of the GitHub Actions secret holding `account`'s PAT. Convention: GH_PAT_<ACCOUNT>[_<QUALIFIER>] with <ACCOUNT> the login upper-snake-cased (e.g. GH_PAT_DON_PETRY). Pre-existing account-named secrets (e.g. DON_PETRY_BOT_GH_PAT) are grandfathered. Must not start with `GITHUB_` (GitHub blocks creation of secrets with that prefix).

evals.description: The held-out eval gate. A persona MUST NOT reach 'stable' (or its declared required_before ring) without an eval set carrying at least min_cases held-out cases — validate-personas.py enforces the count once status reaches required_before. See evals/README.md (dev/holdout split, holdout-guard.yml). Declare EITHER `path` (one eval set) OR `paths` (several, for a persona that wraps multiple skills — e.g. pr-review's deep-review + triage sets); exactly one of the two.

required_before.description: The ring by which the eval set(s) must exist and pass. Recommended: 'stable' at minimum.

path.description: Single eval set — repo-relative path holding dev/ and holdout/ splits. Canonically 'evals/<id>/' so it inherits validate-cases.py + holdout-guard.yml. Use this OR `paths`, not both.

paths.description: Several eval sets, one per skill the persona wraps (e.g. ['evals/deep-review/', 'evals/triage/']). Each holds dev/ + holdout/ splits and must independently clear min_cases. Use this OR `path`, not both. The manifest points at the skill-keyed sets that already exist; it does not fork them.

min_cases.description: Minimum held-out cases required in EACH eval set before promotion to required_before. Enforced by validate-personas.py.

canary.description: OPTIONAL pointer to the ring registry, for a persona that ships its OWN reusable. Per ADR-0006 (.github-private docs/architecture/adr/0006-shared-runtime-personas-are-not-ring-registered.md) a persona served wholly by the SHARED persona runtime (the persona-mention router dispatching to persona-runner) is NOT individually ring-registered — no caller pins a per-persona channel tag — and MUST OMIT this block rather than point at a registry entry that does not exist. Include it only when the persona ships a dedicated reusable, in which case ADR-0002 applies in full. This manifest MUST NOT restate rings, members, or gate knobs — only reference the registry entry by id.

registry.description: Path to the canonical ring registry (petry-projects/.github standards/canary-rings.json).

agent.description: The agents.<key> in canary-rings.json for this persona. MUST equal `id`.

references.description: Relevant docs, ADRs, or issues (e.g. the ADR that introduced this persona).
